For Nigeria’s small businesses, selling to the United States has become a moving target. Tariff costs for buyers have changed four times in the last 18 months, and the latest change brings new challenges for entrepreneurs and business owners. The recent volatility began in April 2025, when the US placed a 14 per cent tax on most Nigerian goods. Four months later, the tariff rate rose to 15 per cent. Then, in February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled these taxes unlawful, and a temporary 10 per cent tax was put in their place. For many exporters, it became difficult to know which rate applied, or for how long. That temporary tax expired in July 2026 and was replaced by the one in place today: a 12.5 per cent tax on goods from countries that, according to the US government, have not banned imports made with forced labour. Nigeria is one of the few African countries on that list. A key concern with the latest tariff is that it falls hardest on small businesses. Nigeria’s largest exports to the US, such as crude oil, gas and fertiliser, are exempt, and those are mostly handled by large enterprises. Beyond these exports, the dividing line tends to fall between raw and finished goods. Most raw commodities, like cocoa beans and raw cashews, are exempt, while finished goods such as roasted cashews, chocolate, shea butter, leather goods, cosmetics, packaged foods and crafts are taxed. These finished goods tend to be items that Nigeria’s small and medium-sized businesses most commonly export. “The greater challenge lies not in the immediate loss of export opportunities, but in navigating an increasingly fragmented and protectionist global trading environment,” Dr Muda Yusuf, Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise (CPPE), said in a policy brief issued after the tax was announced. This growing challenge for small and medium-sized businesses is why Trade Pathways, a US-based, student-run organisation, was founded. Its goal is to create opportunities for small businesses in Africa by giving them free access to the same clear, up-to-date picture of US trade policy that multinationals and large enterprises get from legal teams and policy experts. The platform tracks every US trade policy change and explains the structure in simple terms, so business owners can keep up with the constant shifts and understand buyer behaviour. Having initially served businesses in Kenya and Ghana, Trade Pathways is now launching full coverage for Nigeria, driven by recent trade policy changes and the potential adverse impacts on Nigerian business owners. “Small business owners should be spending their time making and selling great products, not on interpreting US government trade notices,” noted Keshav Suman, the platform’s founder. “The information is public, but it changes constantly and is written for lawyers and policy experts, not for the business owners it affects most.” The timing reflects growing activity among smaller Nigerian exporters. Non-oil exports reached a record $6.1 billion in 2025, and the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC) registered 1,129 new exporters during the year. NEPC’s Executive Director, Nonye Ayeni, has said the council is focused on “reducing dependence on large exporters by supporting small and medium-scale enterprises.” What Nigerian exporting businesses should know now Which party pays the tariff. The US import tax is paid by the American buyer when the goods arrive, not by the Nigerian supplier. Suppliers are still impacted indirectly, however, as buyers ask for lower prices, order smaller quantities, or move part of their orders to suppliers in countries that pay less. The exception is when a seller agrees to deliver goods with all import duties already paid, an arrangement that is common when shipping parcels directly to US customers. In that case, the seller would be responsible for the tax. Product classification. Exemptions from the new tax are set based on product and further classified by process, so two closely related goods can be treated very differently. Raw cashews, for example, are exempt, while roasted cashews are not. Before agreeing on a price, exporters should confirm exactly how their product is classified, so a buyer is not surprised by a higher cost after the order is placed. Refunds of the 2025 tariffs. The emergency tariffs the US charged on imports from around the world in 2025, including the 14 and 15 per cent rates on Nigerian goods, were ruled unlawful by the US Supreme Court in February 2026. US Customs has been refunding importers since April 2026, and on October 8, a US court ruled that importers who have not filed their own lawsuits are covered under a single group claim. Although refunds benefit US buyers, Nigerian export businesses that lowered prices to help buyers absorb the tariff can reasonably negotiate in future pricing discussions. AGOA and duty-free entry. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), a US programme that removes the standard import tax on qualifying goods from sub-Saharan Africa, was extended in September 2026 and now runs until December 2028. It covers thousands of products, including several forms of clothing, footwear, leather goods, processed foods and wooden crafts. Nigeria has also been certified since 2005 to export handloomed and ethnic printed fabrics such as aso oke, Akwete cloth and Ankara prints under AGOA, a benefit that many business owners are not aware of. AGOA does not, however, cancel the new 12.5 per cent tax rate in place for Nigeria. US travel restrictions. Since January 2026, the US government has suspended new business and tourist visas for Nigerian nationals, which makes US trade shows difficult to attend. Video meetings, product samples sent ahead of a call, and US-based sales representatives or partners in the Nigerian diaspora can all help maintain buyer relationships through the absence of physical visits to the US. Alternative markets and customers. Selling to more than one market reduces the risk of depending on a single country’s trade rules. Europe is already Nigeria’s largest buyer of non-oil goods, and many Nigerian products receive reduced import taxes there. Since May 2026, China has charged no import tax on Nigerian goods, an arrangement that runs until April 2028, though food and agricultural exporters must still register with Chinese customs and meet its product standards. Closer to home, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is gradually lowering import taxes between African countries, opening regional markets that are often easier to reach than the US. What comes next Several US developments could change the picture in the coming months. American importers and 25 US states are challenging the current 12.5 per cent tariff in a US trade court, which heard the case on September 30. A potential ruling could reduce or remove the tax entirely, though an appeal is expected on either side. The US government is also expected to announce its annual decisions on which countries remain eligible for AGOA near the end of the year. Trade Pathways noted it is currently tracking each of these policy movements and will update guidance as announcements come. Trade Pathways’ resources for small business owners Trade Pathways provides tools and services that are free for business owners in Kenya, Ghana, and now Nigeria. One such tool is a cost estimator, which calculates what a US buyer would pay at the border for a given product and shipment by country. On a $10,000 shipment, for example, Nigerian cocoa butter costs the buyer about $47 in customs fees, because it is exempt from the current tariff. The same shipment of wooden carvings costs about $1,297, almost all of it the 12.5 per cent tax. item.title: Plateau motorcycle rider killed, mutilated body found
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa A motorcycle rider has been killed by unknown assailants, with his mutilated body reportedly discovered along Longvel Road in Shendam Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victim’s motorcycle was also reportedly stolen, while the circumstances surrounding the killing remained unclear as of the time of filing this report. A resident of the community, Henry Homsuk, told newsmen that “Residents woke up on Monday to the disturbing news of the incident.” “It is sad that someone would be killed and his motorcycle carted away. We woke up to the news this morning, and it was disturbing,” Homsuk said. “It is painful that somebody would lose his life in such circumstances. We are worried about what happened and hope the authorities will take the matter seriously,” he added. ” The issue has been reported to security operatives,” he added “We appeal to the security agencies to investigate this matter thoroughly and ensure that those responsible are arrested.” ” People should be able to go about their lawful activities without fear,” Homsuk said. “Security should be strengthened along Longvel Road and in other vulnerable communities to protect lives and property and prevent a recurrence,” he added. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Alleged phone-tapping: Court rejects El-Rufai’s no-case submission
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday dismissed a no-case submission filed by former Gov. Nasir El-Rufai of Kaduna State in his ongoing trial over alleged unlawful interception of the telephone communications of the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu. Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, in a ruling, held that the Department of State Services (DSS) had placed before the court sufficient evidence to warrant the court to call on the ex-governor to enter his defence if he so desires. The judge, therefore, ordered El-Rufai, the sole defendant in the charge, to enter his defence. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the the defendant had opted for a no-case submission after the DSS closed its case by calling two witnesses. El-Rufai, through his counsel, Akinyemi Aremu, had urged the court to hold that the prosecution had failed to establish a case requiring the former governor to enter a defence. In response, the DSS lawyer, Oluwole Aladedoye, SAN, adopted their counter affidavit in opposition to the no-case submission. Aladedoye argued that the defence failed to address Exhibit “B”, which the prosecution said contained El-Rufai’s alleged admission concerning the tapping of Ribadu’s phone. He submitted that since the prosecution had established a prima facie case against El-Rufai, the defendant was required by law to enter his defence. item.title: No rift between Netanyahu, army chief on Iran – Israel defence minister
item.description: Defence Minister Israel Katz said Monday that reports of a rift between Israel’s army and its civilian leaders over fresh action in the war with Iran were “entirely baseless”. Israel’s Channel 12 reported on Sunday, citing unnamed sources, that there had been a confrontation between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive. The premier dismissed the report as “rubbish” during a TV appearance, and Katz characterised it as an effort to cast doubt on the Netanyahu bloc’s judgement on the eve of close elections. “The reports about gaps between the political echelon and the IDF (army) on the Iran issue are entirely baseless and false,” Katz said on X, insisting there was “complete” coordination between the two. In its report, Channel 12 said Zamir had demanded a detailed discussion as well as legal guarantees and the signatures of the political leadership before carrying out the directive he had received. The outlet did not offer details of the directive, but cited sources saying there were concerns within the army that the war might be exploited for political gain. Katz stated “unequivocally that there was no intention on Israel’s part to initiate an attack on Iran before the elections”. Opposition leader Yair Lapid referenced the report in a post on X Sunday, accusing Netanyahu of seeking to put off the vote. “Tonight it was published that he wants to set off an escalation and a confrontation with Iran, just to postpone the elections,” he said. “This man has lost his grip. We absolutely must send him home.” Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, arguing that only he can finish the job in the US-Israeli war against Iran. item.title: Iran says outcome of Israeli elections ‘makes no difference’
item.description: Iran’s foreign ministry said Monday that the outcome of the Israeli elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing a tight race will make “no difference”. “It makes no difference to us who, in these elections, takes the helm of a regime that has brought nothing but violence and massacres to our region,” said ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing. On Sunday, he told Israel’s Channel 14 that he had “instructed the Mossad and the IDF to overthrow the Iranian regime”. item.title: Ebola: FG confirms evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient, husband to Switzerland
item.description: By Chioma Obinna Nigeria’s index case of imported Ebola virus disease has been evacuated from Abuja to Switzerland after showing significant clinical improvement, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, has said. Pate disclosed this in a post on X, confirming that the evacuation took place earlier on Monday with his approval. He wrote, “I confirm that, with my approval, earlier this morning, the index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease departed Abuja for Switzerland. The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. He, however, cautioned that the patient’s improved condition does not mean she is no longer infectious, stressing that strict public health protocols remain in place. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place,” Pate stated. The patient was evacuated alongside her spouse, who, according to the minister, has remained asymptomatic. Pate expressed appreciation to the clinical staff who cared for the patient and the public health personnel who coordinated the evacuation, commending them for ensuring that the process complied with appropriate public health measures. He said the government would provide further updates later in the afternoon after the patient and her spouse had landed safely at their destination. Reassuring Nigerians that efforts to contain the imported virus were continuing, the minister urged the public to remain vigilant and rely on credible sources of information. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus,” he said. The evacuation marks a further development in Nigeria’s response to the imported Ebola case, with the authorities maintaining that clinical improvement does not remove the need for strict infection prevention and control measures. item.title: Ebola: Suspected index patient evacuated from Nigeria by air ambulance – Report
item.description: A woman reportedly identified as Nigeria’s Ebola index patient has been evacuated from the country by air ambulance, according to a report. The medical evacuation reportedly took place early Monday through the private jet section of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja. According to ARISE News, sources had earlier informed the organisation that the woman, reportedly the wife of a Swiss diplomat in Nigeria, would be flown out of the country at about 6 a.m. Its crew, deployed to the airport’s General Aviation Terminal, reportedly observed a convoy of ambulances and diplomatic vehicles arriving at the private aviation section. The report said airport officials cordoned off the area, while the news organisation later obtained video footage showing a medical evacuation aircraft and its crew preparing to transport a passenger. It said the circumstances surrounding the evacuation led it to suspect that the passenger was the reported Ebola index patient. The report added that a source indicated the Federal Government would announce the evacuation after the aircraft had taken off and left Nigerian airspace. However, the report did not include an official confirmation from the Federal Government, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), or airport authorities establishing the passenger’s identity, diagnosis or destination. The circumstances surrounding the reported evacuation therefore remain subject to official confirmation. Provide accurate information about your movements, contacts, and any symptoms you may have experienced. “Being identified as a contact does not mean that you have Ebola. It means that public health teams need to assess and monitor your health so that any possible infection can be identified early. Your cooperation will help us identify potential cases quickly and prevent further transmission,” Idris added. Marie Bakikula, a caregiver at a UNICEF-supported nursery in Mongbwalu, poses for a photograph in Mongbwalu, north-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, October 10, 2026(Photo by MARIE RUWET / AFP) ‘Our Healthcare Workers’ He commended the healthcare workers whose vigilance and clinical judgement contributed to the identification of this case, noting that their high index of suspicion was critical in triggering the public health response. “I equally recognise their dedication care under challenging circumstances. You are central to our ability to bring this situation under control,” Idris said. “These include not only doctors, nurses and other professionals working in hospitals, but also the public health workforce responsible for surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory diagnosis, case management, infection prevention and control, community engagement and risk communication.” The Director General of the NCDC said the Federal Government would prioritise the safety, health and welfare of health workers throughout the response. “I want to use this opportunity to call on the leadership of every public and private healthcare facility in Nigeria to immediately review and strengthen their infection prevention and control measures. “Screening and triage must be instituted and consistently implemented. item.title: Where is the structure? — OK Movement questions NDC campaign council list
item.description: The Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has questioned the grassroots structure and preparedness of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the 2027 general elections following the party’s unveiling of its National Campaign Council. The Director-General of the OK Movement, John Ughulu, criticised the timing of the announcement, arguing that the party had delayed putting its campaign machinery in place and lacked the grassroots network required to prosecute a nationwide election. Ughulu stated this on Monday in a statement made available to journalists in Abuja, a day after the NDC announced the composition of its campaign council ahead of its inauguration in the Federal Capital Territory. He also boasted that the movement had established a stronger grassroots structure, predicting that some members of the newly announced council would eventually seek its support and mobilisation network. “The funny part of this list is that 90 per cent of the people on it will still come knocking on the doors of the OK Movement to beg for the very structure they have failed to build themselves!” he said. Ughulu further questioned the party’s readiness for the election, challenging its leadership to explain the delay in organising its campaign team. “With less than three months to the general elections, they are only just announcing their Presidential Campaign Council. What exactly have they been doing all this time? Where is the structure? Where is the strategy? Where is the machinery required to prosecute a serious national election?” he asked. The criticism comes amid an escalating disagreement between the NDC and the OK Movement over the movement’s organisational independence and its role in the campaign for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. The NDC on Sunday announced its National Campaign Council, naming its National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, as chairman and Obi as co-chairman. The party’s National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, was appointed vice-chairman, while Kwankwaso was named co-vice-chairman. Other appointees include former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, as chairman of the National Advisory Council; former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege; former presidential candidate, Pat Utomi; and former National Secretary of the Congress for Progressive Change, Buba Galadima. The NDC National Secretary, Ikenna Enekweizu, was named council secretary, while Ibrahim Abdulkarim was appointed Director-General. Ughulu and the OK Movement’s state, local government and ward coordinators were not listed among the appointees. item.title: Gov Radda Pledges Sustained Investment As Katsina Records Decline In Malnutrition Cases
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to sustained investment in nutrition and healthcare, pledging to consolidate the significant progress recorded in reducing malnutrition across the state. Governor Radda gave the assurance on Sunday while receiving nutrition partners operating in Katsina State, led by the Executive Director of the Katsina State Development Management Board (KATDMB), Hajiya Ruqqaya Hamza, at the Government House, Katsina. The Governor said his administration would continue to prioritise nutrition as a critical component of human capital development, while calling on development partners to sustain technical assistance and institutional support to further strengthen the state’s healthcare and nutrition systems. He stressed the need for development organisations to align with the state’s recruitment policy by giving priority to qualified Katsina indigenes in the implementation of their programmes. According to him, building local capacity and integrating skilled professionals into government institutions remain essential for ensuring the long-term sustainability of development interventions. Governor Radda pointed to the Katsina State Development Management Board as an example of the success of such collaborations, noting that several of its personnel were beneficiaries of capacity-building initiatives supported by development partners. He encouraged the organisations to expand investments in human capital development to strengthen local institutions. Earlier, representatives of the nutrition partners presented updates on their interventions across the state during an interactive session. Governor Radda, on Sunday, October 25, 2026, while receiving nutrition partners operating in Katsina State, led by the Executive Director of the Katsina State Development Management Board (KATDMB), Hajiya Ruqqaya Hamza, at the Government House, Katsina. They reported a significant decline in malnutrition cases compared to the previous year, attributing the improvement to the Katsina State Government’s increased investment, strong leadership and unwavering political commitment to nutrition. The partners commended Governor Radda for placing nutrition high on the state’s development agenda and for committing substantial resources to the sector. They also called for deeper collaboration to sustain the gains already achieved and further improve nutrition outcomes across Katsina State. The meeting was attended by representatives of UNICEF, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), ALIMA, International Rescue Committee (IRC), JHPIEGO, Première Urgence Internationale (PUI), International Medical Corps (IMC), Médecins du Monde (MDM), Helen Keller International (HKI), Nutrition International, Save the Children/CGPP and Action Against Hunger. item.title: African players in Europe: Jackson brace ends City’s perfect record
item.description: Senegal star Nicolas Jackson took his goal tally since joining Aston Villa from Chelsea to seven in 11 matches by bagging a brace in a 2-1 Premier League win over Manchester City at the weekend. Victory for Villa ended a seven-match winning streak by City since the league season began. City still top the table, but only on goal difference from defending champions Arsenal. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put Villa ahead in the sixth minute with a fine finish into the roof of the net from John McGinn’s pass. After Erling Haaland equalised for the leaders in the 52nd minute, Jackson clinched a memorable win for Villa eight minutes later. Teenage Senegal international Ibrahim Mbaye teed up Jackson to squeeze his shot past City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. DANGO OUATTARA (Brentford) The Burkina Faso winger scored for the first time this season to rescue a 1-1 draw at Hull City. Ouattara slotted home in the 63rd minute from Igor Thiago’s pass. The 24-year-old cancelled out Oli McBurnie’s first half penalty, but Brentford were left without a win in their last three games. SPAIN INAKI WILLIAMS (Athletic Bilbao) After Spain 2026 World Cup winner Nico Williams came close to scoring, older brother and Ghana international Inaki struck the second goal in a 4-0 La Liga romp against Getafe. A counterattack ended with Inaki Williams one-on-one against the Getafe goalkeeper and he netted with a low shot. ITALY ANDRE-FRANK ANGUISSA (Napoli) Cameroon midfielder Anguissa sent a brilliant bicycle kick into the corner of the net on 28 minutes after Roma failed to clear a free-kick. It was the opening goal of a 3-3 Serie A thriller. GERMANY SERHOU GUIRASSY (Borussia Dortmund) Guirassy was kept off the scoresheet, but posed a constant threat as Borussia beat Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 at home. Early in the opening half, the Guinea international was through on goal, but had his chip saved by goalkeeper Noah Atubolu. Just after the break, Guirassy headed a corner against the bar and went close again when he hit a cross inches wide of the left post. FRANCE ELYE WAHI, SOFIANE DIOP (Nice) Internationals Wahi of the Ivory Coast and Diop of Morocco scored as mid-table Nice came from behind to win 2-1 at Brest in Ligue 1. Wahi equalised just past the hour mark after a corner and Diop punished a defensive blunder to grab the 83rd-minute winner. item.title: Brazil’s Lula clinches poll victory, Bolsonaro seeks to annul election
item.description: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched a re-election victory, but his rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote. With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump. The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied projections to win an unprecedented fourth term. According to official results, he won 51.8 percent of the votes to 48.2 percent for Flavio Bolsonaro, with Lula pulling around 4.4 million more votes. The senator is the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year jail term for attempting a coup after his loss to Lula in the country’s last election in 2022. Sunday’s vote was marked by confusion after a Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours as some polling stations had already closed. The move came at the request of Lula who complained that buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting. Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the decision as “unacceptable” and a “dirty trick” “It is impossible to recognize the results. I am going to request the annulment of these elections,” he said, stone-faced, in a brief speech in Brasilia. No candidate who lost the first round has gone on to win the second in Brazil since 1989, the first direct election after the end of the country’s military dictatorship. “People went to vote because we managed to convince them that voting was very important for ensuring democracy in the country,” Lula said in his first comments after the win. Fireworks and vuvuzelas rang out in Rio de Janeiro, while thousands of people dressed in red, the color of Lula’s Workers’ Party, streamed into the streets of Sao Paulo to celebrate. – Lula’s fight back – After the first-round defeat, the left swung into action with massive rallies, declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro” and revamped their social media strategy. The abstention rate decreased from the first round, falling from 21 percent to 19 percent. Julio Canelo, 42, a lawyer celebrating in Rio de Janeiro hailed a victory for “the entire democratic spectrum.” “It was the result of the people mobilizing, in the streets and online,” he told AFP. A fierce social media battle drew in Meta, parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, which Lula’s campaign accused of favoring his opponent with “algorithmic manipulation.” Meta denied this but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his win. The move came at the request of Lula who complained that buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting. Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the decision as “unacceptable” and a “dirty trick” “It is impossible to recognize the results. The abstention rate decreased from the first round, falling from 21 percent to 19 percent. Julio Canelo, 42, a lawyer celebrating in Rio de Janeiro hailed a victory for “the entire democratic spectrum.” “It was the result of the people mobilizing, in the streets and online,” he told AFP. A fierce social media battle drew in Meta, parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, which Lula’s campaign accused of favoring his opponent with “algorithmic manipulation.” Meta denied this but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his win. A bitter campaign marred by scandals and mudslinging laid bare the deep divisions that have plagued Brazil over the past decade. – A country split in two – Lula heads into a fourth term with almost half of the nation having rejected him, desperate for change. He rose from poverty to become president in 2003 and was re-elected in 2006. Lula made a dramatic return to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months. The charges were annulled on procedural grounds. In his third term, Lula oversaw a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but many voters felt gloomy about the high cost of living and crime. People can barely afford to eat — buying meat is out of the question,” said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro. Lula received congratulations from Chile’s far-right president, Jose Antonio Kast, and Ecuador’s right-wing Daniel Noboa — both close Trump allies. Mexico’s left-wing President Claudia Sheinbaum wrote on X, saying “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won.” The post Brazil’s Lula clinches poll victory, Bolsonaro seeks to annul election appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: See Full List Of NDC Campaign Council Members
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) on Sunday released the list of its newly constituted national campaign council for the 2027 general elections. The list has Senator Seriake Dickson as the chairman, while the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, were listed as co-chairman and co-vice chairman of the national campaign council, respectively. Others are Senator Cleopas Zuwoghe as vice chairman, and former secretary to the government of the federation, Babachir Lawal (National Campaign Advisory Council), as a member. Also on the list are Ikenna Enekweizu, Sidi Abdul, Babatunde Alli, Senator Ovie Omo Agege, Senator Victor Umeh, Ibrahim Abdulkarim (DG, Presidential Campaign), Buba Galadima, Yakubu Ochefu, Mahmud Jahun, Moshood Salvador, Mrs. Dudu Manuga, Victor Ogene, and Muktar Usman. The list also has a 40-member national campaign advisory council and 37 state campaign coordinators. The NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, was named Director of Communication and Media. A former defence spokesperson, Major General John Enenche (retd.), was named Director of Security and Intelligence. The party, in a statement announcing the campaign council on its X handle, said, “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is pleased to announce the constitution of its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections. “The National Campaign Council will provide strategic leadership, coordinate campaign activities across the country, and drive the mobilisation of Nigerians behind the party’s vision of a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria. “The Council will work under the chairmanship of His Excellency, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson CON, NDC National Leader; Co-Chairman, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi CON, our presidential candidate; Vice Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, NDC National Chairman and our vice-presidential candidate, His Excellency, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, Co Vice-Chairman, Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, NDC National Secretary, Council Secretary, and the Director-General, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim to deliver a people-centred and issue-based campaign. “We call on all party members, supporters, and well-meaning Nigerians to remain united and focused as we work together to rescue our country.” See Full List Below: The post See Full List Of NDC Campaign Council Members appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 26, 2026
item.description: The dollar is trading at different rates against the naira across Nigeria’s official foreign exchange market and the parallel market on Monday, October 26, 2026, with the latest available quotations showing differences between the two segments. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official exchange rate was around ₦1,331 per dollar in the latest available market update, while parallel-market dealers quoted rates of approximately ₦1,370 to ₦1,385 per dollar, depending on the location and transaction. Data published by Gatekeepers News on Monday put the official dollar selling rate at ₦1,331.28, while the parallel market recorded a buying rate of ₦1,370 and a selling rate of ₦1,385 per dollar. However, exchange rates vary among banks, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators and other currency dealers, and the actual rate available to customers may differ from published indicative figures. The official foreign exchange market remains a key source of dollar pricing for eligible transactions conducted through authorised channels. The latest available figures for October 26 put the dollar at approximately ₦1,331 per dollar in the official market. This compares with the parallel market, where customers may pay more to purchase physical dollars. International currency data also showed movements in the dollar-naira pair on Monday, although such reference rates do not necessarily match the Central Bank of Nigeria’s official NFEM rate or the rates offered by local currency dealers. In the parallel market, currency dealers were quoting the dollar at approximately ₦1,370 for buying and ₦1,385 for selling, according to the latest market update published on Monday. The buying rate represents the amount dealers pay customers selling dollars, while the selling rate is the amount customers pay when purchasing the US currency. Based on these indicative quotations, $100 would be worth about ₦137,000 when sold to a dealer at the buying rate. Someone purchasing $100 at the selling rate would pay approximately ₦138,500. For $500, the equivalent would be ₦685,000 at the buying rate and ₦692,500 at the selling rate. Meanwhile, $1,000 would exchange for approximately ₦1,370,000 when sold to a dealer or cost ₦1,385,000 to purchase. These calculations are estimates based on published rates. Actual transactions may differ according to dealer pricing, location, dollar availability and the amount exchanged. Movements in the dollar-to-naira exchange rate affect Nigerian businesses and households that depend on imported goods and international payments. A higher dollar rate can increase the naira cost of imported raw materials, machinery, electronics and other products. item.title: Nigeria must manufacture meters locally, secure sustainable financing — Experts
item.description: By Esther Ihejirika Electricity sector experts have called for increased local meter manufacturing, sustainable financing and wider adoption of smart technology to accelerate meter deployment and close Nigeria’s metering gap. They made the call during a webinar on rapid meter rollout, stressing the need for a coordinated national metering plan to improve revenue collection, reduce estimated billing and curb electricity theft. Mr. Odion Omonfoman, host of the webinar, disclosed that the company had achieved “over 90 per cent metering coverage” and deployed more than 200,000 meters through the Meter Asset Provider (MAP) scheme and vendor-financing model. He said the company was targeting 100 per cent metering coverage by extending installations to all customers across its transformers and feeders. “Metering remains a strategic investment in revenue assurance. It enables customers to pay for the electricity they consume while reducing the dissatisfaction associated with estimated billing,” he said. Engr. Alegie Alfred, Head of Metering, Power Limited Electric Company (MPLEC), said Abia Power was tackling energy theft, meter bypass and vandalism through routine inspections, remote monitoring, consumption-pattern analysis, customer education and revenue-protection teams. Speaking on India’s experience, Ms. Ravleen Sethi, Director of Large Corporate Ratings, CareEdge, said government-backed programmes, private-sector investment and improved financing arrangements had accelerated smart-meter deployment in the country. She identified the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), introduced in 2021, as a major driver of investment and expansion in India’s metering manufacturing capacity. From the manufacturing perspective, Engr. Durosola Omogbenigun, President, Meter Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, called for a national metering plan involving the Federal and state governments, electricity distribution companies, investors, regulators and local manufacturers. item.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries declines 6.3% to 15.97mb —NMDPRA
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries declined by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August. This comes as petrol supply from domestic refineries and imports fell sharply during the month. The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday shows that the decline in crude supply coincided with a 23.4 per cent drop in average daily petrol supply to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August. The report attributed the fall in petrol receipts to lower domestic supply and reduced imports as approved import permit volumes were being exhausted. Between January and September 2026, refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude. Domestic production accounted for 80.4 per cent of total intake, while imported cargoes contributed 19.6 per cent. The report further showed that Dangote Refinery’s utilisation stood at 105.98 per cent in September, implying crude processing of approximately 689,000 barrels per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day. The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from refinery inventory, indicating that the refinery processed more crude than it received during the month. Despite the September decline, domestic refineries remained the larger source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts during the month, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports. The September total was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026. Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres per day, accounting for 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent. The NMDPRA said September petrol receipts declined as domestic supply fell 21 per cent below August levels, while imports dropped by 30 per cent amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes.
